source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 2. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.
topic: Washing away what is impure before prayer

learn.en: Najāsah is something impure, like urine (wee) and stool (poo). A Muslim washes it away before praying.
learn.title: What is najāsah?

learn.en: If any of it touches your body, your clothes or your prayer place, wash that spot with water until it is gone. Then it is clean again.
learn.title: Wash it away

learn.en: Cleaning yourself with water after using the toilet is called istinjāʾ. If there is no water, clean tissue can be used.
learn.title: After the toilet

learn.en: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ: “And your clothing purify.” (Qur'an 74:4) And the Prophet ﷺ said: “Purity is half of faith.” (Muslim 223)
learn.title: Half of faith

learn.en: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to be careful with urine and not to let it splash on us. Being careless with it is not a small thing. (Bukhari 218)
learn.title: Be careful

quiz.en: What do we do if urine touches our clothes?
True or false? Purity is half of faith.
True or false? Istinjāʾ means cleaning yourself after using the toilet.
True or false? It does not matter if urine splashes on us.

think.q: Your little brother spills juice and wee on your trousers just before Dhuhr. What do you do, step by step?
think.a: Wash the spot with water until it is gone (or change your trousers), make wudu if you need to, then pray.

parents.summary: Najāsah (like urine and stool) must be washed off the body, clothes and prayer place with water. Istinjāʾ is cleaning after the toilet. Purity is half of faith.
parents.tip: Practise the bathroom routine together: water, left hand, wash hands well after.
